transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Uh, hi. I guess... I'm just here because I get pulled off track a lot. By just, like, every little sound or thought. 

If I'm trying to work on an application or something, a car going by outside or my phone will just... send me somewhere else. I don't really even notice it happening until later. So, yeah. That's mostly it.
Can you tell me how far back these problems with distraction go — did you notice them as far back as childhood, like in elementary school, or did they start more recently in adulthood?

Uh... yeah, a long time. Like, even back in elementary school, I guess. Teachers were always... moving my seat around. Just because I'd talk out of turn, or... forget my homework. And when I did the worksheets, I'd just kind of rush through them and make careless mistakes. So... yeah. It goes back that far.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about different things most days, even when there's no clear reason to worry?
Um... no. Not really. I don't think so. I mean, I get stressed if something is actually going wrong, I guess. But I don't just sit around worrying for no reason.
Do you often feel restless, fidgety, or have trouble sitting still, or find yourself acting impulsively—like interrupting others or making quick decisions without thinking them through?

Um... yeah, I guess. I don't really sit completely still. Like, if I'm sitting with someone, my leg is usually bouncing... or I'm clicking a pen, or just messing with my keys. I don't really even realize I'm doing it most of the time. So... yeah.
Do you often find yourself interrupting other people when they're talking, or blurting out answers or comments before someone finishes speaking?

Yeah... I guess I do that. Um, I cut people off a lot. Like, especially my mom... or my counselor. An answer just kind of pops into my head, and I just say it. Before they're even done talking. So... yeah.
Do these attention and impulsivity issues cause noticeable problems for you in more than one area of your life—for example, both at work or school and at home or in relationships?

Yeah, I guess so. I mean... it definitely messes things up. Like with work stuff. I'm trying to become an automotive technician, but... I keep missing deadlines for the training stuff. Or I mess up the applications and have to do them over. It's frustrating because... I know I can do the actual hands-on work. I just... can't seem to get past all the other stuff. So, yeah, it causes problems.
